items.title: Arthur Baron interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 3, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: He was in his late 90s when we were doing these gigs... the last gig he did I believe was with my band at an open air church gig down here at St. Mark’s Church.

ctx.x: I’m wondering if you were close to any of them. © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

A lot of them. Bucky Pizzarelli. Bucky had a lot of, a lot of friends. I’m not claiming sole ownership, you know, and I didn’t see him that much, but as he got older, I met him in a recording session a zillion years ago and he always remembered me. Months could go by and I started — for a while there was this organization at Lincoln Center, not even actually part of Jazz at Lincoln Center, it was PTSPD — not the post traumatic syndrome but similar letters. And they got a lot of nursing home gigs and things like…
Whatever you got give me some.
